summary: This mishnah teaches what time the afternoon korban tamid was brought on a regular day, and how it was moved earlier on Erev Pesach.

chunks.en: The tamid is shechted at eight and a half hours
chunks.explain: Hours of the day, counting from morning.
chunks.st: The daily afternoon offering is slaughtered at eight and a half hours of the day, which is two and a half hours after midday,

words.note: The korban brought every day, morning and afternoon.

chunks.en: and offered at nine and a half.
chunks.st: and is sacrificed, i.e., its offering on the altar is completed, at nine and a half hours of the day.

chunks.en: On Erev Pesach it is shechted at seven
chunks.explain: It is earlier, so there is time for the korban Pesach after it.
chunks.st: On the eves of Passover, when the Paschal lamb must be offered after the daily offering, the daily offering is sacrificed earlier; it is slaughtered at seven and a half hours

chunks.en: and a half, and offered at eight and a half,
chunks.st: and sacrificed at eight and a half hours,

chunks.en: whether on a weekday or on Shabbos.
chunks.st: whether it occurs during the week or on Shabbat.

chunks.he: חָל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: If Erev Pesach falls on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.explain: Then the korban Pesach must be roasted before Shabbos.
chunks.st: If Passover eve occurs on Shabbat eve,
chunks.stMore: when the Paschal lamb must be offered even earlier to ensure that it will be roasted before the onset of Shabbat,

chunks.he: נִשְׁחָט בְּשֵׁשׁ וּמֶחֱצָה וְקָרֵב בְּשֶׁבַע וּמֶחֱצָה,
chunks.en: it is shechted at six and a half and offered at seven and a half,
chunks.st: the daily offering is slaughtered at six and a half hours and sacrificed at seven and a half hours,

chunks.en: and the korban Pesach comes after it.
chunks.st: and the Paschal lamb is offered thereafter.

summary: A korban Pesach must be brought for its own sake. If it is done for a different korban, even in part, it is not kosher.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that was shechted not for its own sake,
chunks.explain: He said he was shechting it as a different korban.
chunks.st: The Paschal lamb that the priest slaughtered not for its own purpose,
chunks.stMore: i.e., at the time of slaughter he said that his intent was to slaughter it as a different offering, e.g., a peace-offering or burnt-offering, rather than as a Paschal lamb;

chunks.en: or he caught the blood, carried it, or threw it not for its own sake,
chunks.st: or if the priest received the blood, or carried the blood to the altar, or sprinkled the blood on the altar while saying that it was not for the purpose of the Paschal lamb;

words.note: Caught the blood in a bowl.
Threw the blood on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: or for its own sake and not for its own sake,
chunks.st: or if the priest performed the rites both for its own purpose and not for its own purpose;

chunks.en: or not for its own sake and for its own sake,
chunks.st: or not for its own purpose and for its own purpose;

chunks.en: it is not kosher. What is "for its own sake and not for its own sake"?
chunks.st: in all these cases, the Paschal lamb is disqualified. How does one perform the rites for its own purpose and not for its own purpose?

chunks.en: For a korban Pesach and for a shelamim.
chunks.st: It is in a case where the priest said that his intent is for the purpose of the Paschal lamb and for the purpose of a peace-offering.

chunks.en: What is "not for its own sake and for its own sake"?
chunks.st: And how does one perform rites not for its own purpose and for its own purpose?

chunks.en: For a shelamim and for a korban Pesach.
chunks.st: It is in a case where the priest says that the offering is for the purpose of a peace-offering and for the purpose of a Paschal lamb.

summary: This mishnah teaches for whom the korban Pesach must be shechted, and at what time of day.

chunks.en: If he shechted it not for the people who will eat it, and not for those signed up for it,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered the Paschal lamb for people who cannot eat it or for those who did not register in advance to eat it,

words.note: People who signed up to eat this korban.

chunks.en: or for people without a bris, or for people who are tamei,
chunks.explain: The Torah does not let them eat the korban Pesach.
chunks.st: or if one slaughtered it for people who are uncircumcised or for those who are ritually impure, whom the Torah prohibits from eating the Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: it is not kosher. For those who will eat it and for those who won't,
chunks.st: it is disqualified. However, if one slaughtered it for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it;

chunks.en: for those signed up and for those not signed up,
chunks.st: for those who have registered for it and for those who have not registered for it;

chunks.en: for those with a bris and for those without,
chunks.st: for the circumcised and for the uncircumcised;

words.en: and for those without a bris

chunks.en: for those who are tamei and for those who are tahor,
chunks.st: for the ritually impure and for the ritually pure,

chunks.en: it is kosher. If he shechted it before midday,
chunks.explain: Only part of his plan was wrong, so it still counts.
chunks.st: it is valid, for a partially invalid intent does not disqualify the offering. If one slaughtered the Paschal lamb before midday

chunks.he: פָּסוּל, מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות יב) בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם.
chunks.en: it is not kosher, because it says, "in the afternoon."
chunks.st: it is disqualified, as it is stated: “And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it in the afternoon” (Exodus 12:6).

chunks.en: If he shechted it before the tamid,
chunks.st: If he slaughtered it before the daily afternoon offering

chunks.he: כָּשֵׁר, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא אֶחָד מְמָרֵס בְּדָמוֹ
chunks.en: it is kosher, as long as someone keeps stirring its blood
chunks.explain: So that the blood does not get thick.
chunks.st: it is valid, as long as another person stirs its blood in order to prevent it from congealing

chunks.en: until the blood of the tamid is thrown.
chunks.st: until the blood of the daily offering is sprinkled.

chunks.en: And if it was thrown first, it is kosher.
chunks.st: And if the blood of the Paschal lamb is sprinkled before the blood of the daily offering, it is nonetheless valid, as this change does not disqualify the offering.

summary: The Torah says not to shecht the korban Pesach while owning chametz. The Tanna'im argue which korbanos this mitzvah is about.

chunks.en: One who shechts the korban Pesach while he has chametz
chunks.st: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leavened bread still in his possession

chunks.en: breaks a "do not" mitzvah.
chunks.st: violates a negative commandment,
chunks.stMore: as the Torah states: “You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread; neither shall the sacrifice of the festival of Passover be left until the morning” (Exodus 34:25).

words.note: A mitzvah that says not to do something.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: also the tamid.
chunks.st: Even one who slaughters the daily afternoon offering on Passover eve with leaven in his possession violates the commandment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: the korban Pesach on the fourteenth:
chunks.st: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb on the fourteenth of Nisan

chunks.en: for its own sake, he is guilty,
chunks.st: for its own purpose with leaven in his possession is liable;

chunks.en: and not for its own sake, he is free.
chunks.st: but if he slaughtered it for a different purpose he is exempt.

chunks.en: And all other korbanos,
chunks.st: And for all other offerings that one slaughters on Passover eve, when owning leaven is prohibited,

chunks.en: whether for their own sake or not for their own sake,
chunks.st: whether he slaughtered them for their own purpose or he slaughtered them for a different purpose,

chunks.en: he is free. And during the Moed,
chunks.st: he is exempt. And during the festival of Passover,

chunks.en: for its own sake, he is free,
chunks.explain: It is not a kosher korban at this time, so it does not count.
chunks.st: if one slaughtered the Paschal lamb for its own purpose he is exempt.
chunks.stMore: Since a Paschal lamb that is slaughtered for its own purpose at an improper time is disqualified, it is not an offering at all and there is no violation of the commandment: “You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread.”

chunks.en: and not for its own sake, he is guilty.
chunks.st: However, if he slaughtered it for a different purpose and thereby validated the sacrifice as a peace-offering, he is liable for having sacrificed it with leaven in his possession.

chunks.en: And all other korbanos,
chunks.st: And for all other offerings that one slaughters on Passover, when it is prohibited to slaughter with leaven in one’s possession,

chunks.en: whether for their own sake or not for their own sake,
chunks.st: whether he slaughtered them for their own purpose or he slaughtered them for a different purpose,

chunks.he: חַיָּב, חוּץ מִן הַחַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ:
chunks.en: he is guilty, except for a chatas that he shechted not for its own sake.
chunks.st: he is liable. This is with the exception of a sin-offering that he slaughtered for a different purpose with leaven in his possession.
chunks.stMore: Unlike other offerings, a sin-offering is disqualified if it is slaughtered for a different purpose, and therefore one does not violate the prohibition of “You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread.”

words.note: A korban brought for a sin.

summary: The korban Pesach was shechted in three groups. This mishnah describes how the first group came into the Beis Hamikdash, and how the Kohanim stood with their bowls.

chunks.en: The korban Pesach is shechted in three groups,
chunks.st: The Paschal lamb was slaughtered in three groups,
chunks.stMore: meaning those bringing the offering were divided into three separate sets,

chunks.en: as it says, "And they shall shecht it, all
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And the whole

chunks.en: the assembly of the congregation of Israel":
chunks.st: assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it in the afternoon” (Exodus 12:6).

chunks.en: (Shemos 12) assembly, congregation, and Israel.
chunks.st: The verse is interpreted as referring to three groups: Assembly, congregation, and Israel.
chunks.stMore: The procedure for sacrificing the offering was as follows:

chunks.en: The first group came in,
chunks.st: The first group of people sacrificing the offering entered,

chunks.en: the Azarah became full,
chunks.st: and when the Temple courtyard became filled with them

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis Hamikdash.

chunks.en: they locked the doors of the Azarah.
chunks.st: they closed the doors of the Temple courtyard.

chunks.en: They blew tekiah, teruah, and tekiah.
chunks.st: They sounded uninterrupted, broken, and uninterrupted trumpet blasts, as was done while sacrificing any offering.

chunks.en: The Kohanim stood in rows and rows,
chunks.st: The priests stood in rows from the place of slaughter to the altar,

chunks.en: and in their hands were silver bowls and gold bowls.
chunks.explain: To catch the blood of the korbanos.
chunks.st: and in their hands they held bowls [bezikhin] of silver and bowls of gold in order to receive the blood of the offerings.

chunks.en: A row that was all silver, silver,
chunks.st: There was a row entirely composed of priests holding silver bowls,

chunks.en: and a row that was all gold, gold.
chunks.st: and a row entirely composed of priests holding gold bowls,

chunks.en: They were not mixed.
chunks.st: as the gold and silver bowls were not mixed in the same row.

chunks.en: And the bowls did not have flat bottoms,
chunks.st: The bowls did not have flat bases that would allow them to be put down,

chunks.en: so that they would not put them down and the blood would get thick.
chunks.explain: Then it could not be thrown on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: out of concern that perhaps the priests would set them down and forget about them and in the meantime the blood would congeal and become disqualified for sprinkling on the altar.

summary: This mishnah describes how the blood of the korban Pesach was passed from Kohen to Kohen until it was thrown on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: A Yisrael shechted it, and a Kohen caught the blood,
chunks.st: An Israelite would slaughter the sacrifice, and a priest would receive the blood and immediately

words.note: A Jew who is not a Kohen.

chunks.en: he gives it to his friend, and his friend to his friend,
chunks.st: hand it to another priest standing next to him, and the other priest would pass it to another.

chunks.he: וּמְקַבֵּל אֶת הַמָּלֵא וּמַחֲזִיר אֶת הָרֵיקָן.
chunks.en: and he takes the full one and gives back the empty one.
chunks.st: Each priest would receive a full bowl of blood from the priest next to him and return to him an empty bowl being passed in the opposite direction, the contents of which had already been sprinkled on the altar.

chunks.en: The Kohen closest to the mizbe'ach throws it
chunks.st: The priest who was closest to the altar would sprinkle

chunks.en: with one throw toward the base.
chunks.st: a single sprinkling of blood against the base of the altar, i.e., against the north and west sides of the altar, where there was a base.

words.note: The bottom step of the mizbe'ach.

summary: This mishnah tells how the second and third groups did the same as the first, and how everyone said Hallel while the korbanos were shechted.

chunks.he: יָצְתָה כַת רִאשׁוֹנָה וְנִכְנְסָה כַת שְׁנִיָּה.
chunks.en: The first group went out and the second group came in.
chunks.st: The first group exited upon completion of the rite, and the second group entered;

chunks.en: The second went out,
chunks.st: the second group left upon completion of its rite,

chunks.en: the third came in.
chunks.st: and the third group entered.

chunks.he: כְּמַעֲשֵׂה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה כָּךְ מַעֲשֵׂה הַשְּׁנִיָּה וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁית.
chunks.en: Just as the first did, so did the second and the third.
chunks.st: As it was done by the first group, so was it done by the second and third groups.

chunks.en: They said Hallel.
chunks.st: All the people standing in the Temple courtyard while the Paschal lambs were being slaughtered would recite hallel.

chunks.en: If they finished, they said it a second time,
chunks.st: If they finished reciting it before all the offerings were slaughtered, they recited it a second time,

chunks.en: and if they finished a second time, they said it a third time,
chunks.st: and if they finished reciting it a second time, they recited it a third time,

words.en: they did it a third time

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שִׁלְּשׁוּ מִימֵיהֶם.
chunks.en: even though they never said it a third time.
chunks.explain: The Kohanim worked fast, so they finished first.
chunks.st: although in practice they never recited it a third time, as the priests worked efficiently and finished the rite before this became necessary.

words.en: they did it a third time

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: the third group never
chunks.st: The third group never reached even once the opening verse of the fourth chapter of hallel: “

chunks.en: reached "I love that Hashem hears,"
chunks.explain: A pasuk in the middle of Hallel.
chunks.st: I love that the Lord hears the voice of my supplications” (Psalms 116:1),

chunks.en: because it had few people.
chunks.st: because its people were few and the slaughtering of all the offerings was completed during the recitation of the first three chapters.

summary: The korban Pesach was brought the same way on Shabbos. This mishnah tells how the Kohanim washed the Azarah, and what Rabbi Yehuda says about the blood on the floor.

chunks.en: Just as it is done on a weekday, so it is done on Shabbos,
chunks.st: As it was done during the week, so was it done on Shabbat;

chunks.en: except that the Kohanim washed
chunks.st: only that on Shabbat the priests would rinse

chunks.en: the Azarah, which the Sages did not want.
chunks.explain: They did it on Shabbos too, like on a weekday.
chunks.st: the Temple courtyard, cleaning away the blood, contrary to the wishes of the Sages,
chunks.stMore: as the priests did not want to veer from the weekday procedure in this regard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: a Kohen would fill a cup from the mixed blood,
chunks.explain: Blood of many korbanos, mixed on the floor.
chunks.st: Before the floor was rinsed, a priest would fill a cup with the blood of the many offerings brought that day that was now mixed together on the floor and then

chunks.he: זְרָקוֹ זְרִיקָה אַחַת עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
chunks.en: and throw it with one throw on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: sprinkle it with a single sprinkling upon the altar.

chunks.en: But the Sages did not agree with him.
chunks.st: But the Rabbis did not agree with Rabbi Yehuda with regard to this point.

summary: This mishnah describes where people hung up their korban Pesach to take off its skin.

chunks.en: How did they hang up the korban and take off its skin?
chunks.st: How would one suspend and flay the Paschal lamb in the Temple?

chunks.en: There were iron hooks
chunks.st: Iron hooks [unkelayot] were

chunks.en: fixed in the walls and in the pillars,
chunks.st: secured into the walls and pillars,

chunks.en: on which they would hang and take off the skin.
chunks.st: and upon them one would suspend the offering and flay it.

chunks.en: And anyone who did not have
chunks.st: If anyone lacked

chunks.en: a place to hang and take off the skin,
chunks.st: a place among the hooks in the Temple courtyard to suspend and flay the offering,

words.en: and to take off the skin

chunks.en: there were thin, smooth sticks there,
chunks.st: there were thin, smooth rods there,

chunks.he: וּמֵנִיחַ עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְעַל כֶּתֶף חֲבֵרוֹ,
chunks.en: and he would put one on his shoulder and on his friend's shoulder,
chunks.st: which he would place on his own shoulder and on another’s shoulder,

chunks.en: and hang it and take off the skin.
chunks.st: and from it he would suspend the offering and flay it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: when the fourteenth falls on Shabbos,
chunks.explain: Then they may not carry the sticks.
chunks.st: When the fourteenth of Nisan occurred on Shabbat, when moving the rods is prohibited (Rambam),

chunks.en: he puts his hand on his friend's shoulder,
chunks.st: he would rest his hand on another’s shoulder

chunks.en: and his friend's hand on his shoulder,
chunks.st: and the other’s hand on his own shoulder

chunks.en: and hangs it and takes off the skin.
chunks.st: and suspend the offering and flay it.

summary: This mishnah tells how the parts of the korban Pesach were burned on the mizbe'ach, and where the groups waited when Erev Pesach was on Shabbos.

chunks.en: He tore it open and took out the parts for the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: He would tear open the flesh of the offering and remove its sacrificial parts, i.e., the fats and other parts offered on the altar.

words.note: The fats burned on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.he: נְתָנוֹ בְמָגִיס וְהִקְטִירָן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
chunks.en: put them in a large bowl, and burned them on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: He would place the sacrificial parts in a large basin [mageis] and burn them on the altar.

chunks.en: The first group went out and sat
chunks.explain: On Shabbos, they could not carry the korban home.
chunks.st: If this took place on Shabbat, when carrying is prohibited, the first group would exit and

chunks.en: on Har Habayis,
chunks.st: remain on the Temple Mount;

chunks.en: the second in the Cheil,
chunks.st: the second group would remain within the rampart, which was an area outside the women’s courtyard;

words.note: An area just outside the Azarah.

chunks.en: and the third stood in its place.
chunks.st: and the third group would stand in its place in the Temple.

chunks.en: When it got dark, they went out and roasted their korbanos Pesach.
chunks.st: They would wait there until nightfall, and as soon as it became dark, they would all go out and roast their Paschal lambs, everyone in his own place.
